` inside a table cell's `{> …}` description that is not written `\

`. A table row splits on every unescaped pipe before the chart reads the cell, so the pipe ends the description early and adds a cell: the row has more cells than its header and every value after the description shifts one column. The fix is `\
` inside the description, or rewording it. A `
` in a list row's `>` description is just text and is not checked.

A series name spelled two ways across the groups of a nested bar, line, stacked-bar, slope or radar list (`Licenses` under one group, `Licences` under the next). head: Rule ID
Severity
Autofix
What it catches
body: A `_class` token that is not a known component or modifier, or one that was renamed. Carries a did-you-mean.
Two tokens on one slide from an axis that takes one value at a time (two variants, two finishes); only one wins.
An editorial modifier (`insight-*`, `no-note`) on a layout that has nothing for it to act on.

On a list slide, a counter modifier its register never reads: `numbered` without `takeaway`, or `lettered`/`roman`/`bullet` without `principles`. Also `principles` over `-` bullets (it numbers an ordered list only), and `takeaway` over a `1.` list without `numbered` (the numbers are hidden).
`- **Title.** body` (or ordered `1. **Title.** body`) on a card-style layout — the body inherits the parent `li` bold. Fix: nested `- Title` / `  - body`.
The unordered inline-bold shape on a ledger/numbered layout — autofixes to the ordered `1. Name` / `   - body` shape the layout wants.

A `>` at the left margin between two items of a chart's list. It ends the list, so every row after it drops out of the chart. On a chart that reads a row's `>` (flowchart, state-chart and the 13 detail charts) the fix indents a one-line quote under the item above, where it becomes that row's description (a quote of several lines gets no machine fix: indent each line by hand); on a list chart that reads no detail under its rows there is no machine fix.

A `>` under a row with no mark of its own: a radar series (its marks are its axes) or a quadrant group (its marks are its points). The chart lifts it out, so it is shown nowhere; move it under an axis or a point, where it is that mark's description.

A value in a chart's rows or cells that is shaped like a number but is not one: two signs (`--5`, `(-5)`), an unpaired parenthesis (`(5`, `5)`), or digits that are not one number (`1,2,3`, `1.2.3.4x`). The chart reads it as no value (a point chart draws no mark, a pie wedge or funnel stage reads as zero, a bullet prints it as typed); before, each read as a different number with no warning. Only charts that read numbers check it, so a dotted date on a timeline is not flagged. Which number was meant is the author's call, so there is no machine fix.

A chart's data row written as one `{…}` record (``- Uptime `{4.2M, target=5.0M}` ``) that the chart cannot draw: the record holds a field the chart cannot draw (none on a native chart, bullet or progress, which read every field; a value no single-backtick span can hold on another), it is followed on its row by a quote the chart does not read or another paragraph (a native chart reads a record only when it ends the row's first line, as old spans must), it follows another code span on the row (`` `1` `{2}` ``), it sits in a later paragraph of its row, or on the line after a heading item (the old spans draw a value there, the record is read only from the row's first line, so it stays a pill), it is a plain number under a row that has a value (stacked-bar's segment under a total: the old form reads it as a segment, the record as a note), or the chart's row schema refuses it and it is not a pill either (`{3, targt=5}`: a typo that used to drop the row from the chart), it sits in a chart list inside a `>` quote (the old spans draw there, a record does not), or a badge before the row's label holds a value too, as a record or a plain number (`` `{1}` North `{40}` ``, `` `1` North `{40}` ``: the chart reads neither; `{1, circle}` reads as a badge). A record in a `>` quote that is a row's description is not checked: neither form draws a row there. A record with an old form draws, because the chart family rewrites it to the spans each chart reads. Scatter and quadrant read a record directly and are not checked; a nested bullet under a row that has a value is detail on a chart that reads it so, and is not checked, except bullet's keyword rows (`Target`, `Plan`, `Floor`, `Band` and the rest of its keywords) written as records, which the bullet reads as a note. There is no machine fix, because the model's codemod writes the record form.
` inside a table cell's `{> …}` description that is not written `\

`. A table row splits on every unescaped pipe before the chart reads the cell, so the pipe ends the description early and adds a cell: the row has more cells than its header and every value after the description shifts one column. The fix is `\
` inside the description, or rewording it. A `
` in a list row's `>` description is just text and is not checked.

A series name spelled two ways across the groups of a nested bar, line, stacked-bar, slope or radar list (`Licenses` under one group, `Licences` under the next). The chart matches series by their text, so the odd spelling draws a second series. The two names differ only in case or spacing, or by one small edit, and never share a group, and the groups show a shared shape (each group holding the odd spelling also holds another series, and each of those appears under the intended spelling's groups; a case or spacing difference needs no such evidence). Only rows the chart draws as a series point (a number last) in the slide's first list count; a note row is never renamed. A difference only in digits (`Q1`, `Q2`), or in a one- or two-letter last word (`Plan A`, `Plan B`, `UK`, `US`), is a different series, because a series missing from a group is a supported shape. The fix rewrites the spelling used under fewer groups to the one used under more (the first group's, on a tie).

A `{> prose}` description where the chart does not read one. In a list row it is not read, and written after the row's record it leaves the row with no value (`- North `{40}` `{> grew fast}`` draws no bar); a list row's description is a `>` quote indented under it. On a chart whose rows take a quote the fix moves the prose into that quote; elsewhere, and for a description in a table cell of a chart that does not read one (only heatmap does), the finding has no fix On a heatmap table it also warns on a header description with no column name before it (the whole span is then the column's name), a `{>}` that shares its header cell, a second `{>}` column (dropped), a description in the label column or in the `{>}` column (read as its own text).
A `**bold**` span inside an ordered-list statement, which splits the counter-grid row (e.g. `principles`).
A right-panel item with no nested body on a split layout — the title won't lift to bold.
An h2-anchored split slide (`split-panel`/`split-compare`) with no `## ` headline — the left panel renders empty.
A `split-panel pullquote` with no `> ` blockquote — the pull-quote (the variant's point) renders empty.
`split-compare` without exactly two top-level options — the layout assumes a two-up and highlights the 2nd as preferred.
A `kpi`/`stats` number item with no nested label — the number won't render in display type.
A `big-number` slide whose number is written as a heading, so the required number slot (the first list item) is empty.
A bleeding claim (a per-slide `claim-*` or the deck-wide `claim:`) on a component that excludes it (a prose-dense or table layout), whose content is cropped at the true edge.
A `qr` payload bullet with no value.
A `qr` slide with no scannable payload bullet.
A `qr` slide with more than one payload bullet; it renders only one.
A `collage` with fewer than four or more than six photos; past six the tiles are too small to read and the layout falls back to an even grid.
A `collage` photo with no alt text, which is the screen-reader label and the label in the enlarged view.
A `collage` that uses `![bg](…)` background syntax, which belongs to `image`; a collage lists inline photos one per bullet.

A trailing hint span after a `collage` photo that is not `hero`, one focal word (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `center`) and a ratio such as `3:2`; the whole span is ignored and nothing is drawn for it.
Text after a `collage` photo that is not a clean hint span; a collage draws no per-photo text, and any hint on that line is ignored.
More than one `collage` photo marked `hero`; only the first counts.

A bare `track:` (deck-wide from that slide on) where `_track:` was meant, `_track` on a slide that is not `topic` or on `topic fact`, a track with fewer than two labels (none is drawn), or a track with no current topic.
A list on a `topic` slide, which shows as plain content; the track is built from the section's headings.
A malformed `_focus` directive; it silently does nothing at render.
A `_focusStyle` value that is not `spotlight`, `ring`, `list-fill`, `blur` or `highlight`.
A `_focusSteps` step that is not a valid `_focus` spec (only the first bad step is reported).
A `map` list item whose lead name the basemap can't resolve. Carries a did-you-mean against the basemap vocabulary.
A `map highlight` slide whose values are labels (or absent), so the data already fills it by category and the class says nothing.
A word in an `authority-chain trail` column too long for the column, which squeezes the others.
On `decision` and `compare-prose` (not `axis`), a card tag long enough to wrap, or a band label long enough to run past two lines, which grows every tag on the slide and pushes the cards down.
A `![bg left]` / `![bg right]` (or a ratio) on a slide that is not `image`: only the image layout places a picture beside the text, so it fills the whole slide behind it instead.
A ratio such as `![bg left:40%]` on an `image` slide: the ratio is not read, so the slide falls back to a full-bleed background and loses its panel.
A label list naming key entries, placed above the chart: there it names the axes instead of relabeling the key, or shows as text if it has more items than the chart has axes.
A bracketed label list that relabels nothing: on a component with no key, an entry that is not one of the component's key members, or a key named twice (the last wins).
A `shell` (or similar) fence holding a script; the language only colors terminal prompts, so it renders nearly plain.
An `@code{…}` record above a fence that does not read: an unknown word, a bad line range, a width out of range. The render ignores what it cannot read.
An `@code{…}` record line with no fence after it, so it configures nothing and renders as inline code.

A line reference past the end of its code block: `focus=` or `mark=` in a record, or a slide's `_focus: line` against its first fence. It marks nothing. Not checked on a formatted block, whose lines the formatter decides.
A block whose own `@code{…}` record asks for `format` in a language no formatter reads; it keeps its text.
